normalisation: route is compared as {destination,state,boundary_reason}; boundary_reason is populated only for provisional_boundary. This retains evidence_gate, formula_conflict, mixed_promise, li_g0_provisional and pending_leave_in_addendum; committed and held are never folded together. Non-boundary pair/reason vocabulary remains calculation log.
application_moment compares primary only: {primary,also[]} versus string. also[] is excluded as requested. provides_heat_protection compares the boolean value, not research-trace wrappers.
buildup/alcohol notes: false, {fired:false}, not_fired and does_not_fire -> does_not_fire; true, {fired:true}, fired and fires -> fires. null remains null.

Set-valued arrays (secondary_jobs, mechanisms, review_triggers, flags) are deduplicated and sorted. Object keys are sorted for comparison. Free prose and rule-path order remain log differences, not behavioural defects.
neutral_fact folds whitespace, typographic quotation marks and case as round 4. Tail INCI folds case, whitespace and Parfum/Fragrance aliases; rank/status remain visible, T_S.alt is diagnostic-only.

lock_rules.quote: | R3-L | **Lock criterion „lanes agree" (PH1-11) means resolved, not identical.** Styling v1.0 may lock when every remaining A/B disagreement is resolved — either a lane error proven against a clear rule, or the rule gap behind it closed — **and** a final confirmation round shows only lane errors and no new rule gaps. Literal identity of both lanes on every value is not required. |

| R4-L | **Lock scope under R3-L: only differences in user-facing fields block the lock** — route/recommendability (incl. held vs committed, evidence gate), subtype, hold level, weight, finish, flexibility, target zone, application moment, primary and secondary jobs, heat protection, user-shown notes. Differences confined to the **calculation log** (reason code, rule path, internal review triggers, confidence, internal flags, lexicon placements that move no value) do not block: they are fixed in the text and documented, without a further round. Example: Bali Curls Sleek Stick — both lanes agree on every user field; only reason code and rule path differ. |

rules.quote: | R8-Q2 | **The product noun „Puder"/„Powder" names the `volume` job** (owner, after a cohort check: all 10 hair powders promise volume, 7 also texture/grip, almost always alongside volume). Texture/grip counts as a secondary job where a C1/C2 line promises it; a name that itself names grip (Redken „Powder Grip") is a two-job name and falls to its lead line. rules.matched_fragment: texture/grip promised in a C1/C2 line is an eligible secondary
rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2, R8-Q2]`:** Puder/Powder states `volume`; texture/grip promised in a C1/C2 line is an eligible secondary, subject to the same order and formula gate. Redken „Powder Grip“ is a two-job name (volume + texture) and the lead line decides primary. Other product-noun mappings stay unchanged: „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a molding/hold product noun (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) states `hold_fix` and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true word for a different job beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl; Grip beside Powder) makes a two-job name (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2, R8-Q2]`:** Puder/Powder states `volume`; texture/grip promised in a C1/C2 line is an eligible secondary, subject to the same order and formula gate. Redken „Powder Grip“ is a two-job name (volume + texture) and the lead line decides primary. Other product-noun mappings stay unchanged: „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a molding/hold product noun (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) states `hold_fix` and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true word for a different job beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl; Grip beside Powder) makes a two-job name (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

Redken „Powder Grip“ is a two-job name (volume + texture) and the lead line decides primary.
